messages:
maya: Morning — blocking upgrade to runtime:2.4.0 in eu-west. Pods failing to schedule on GPU nodes after chart rollout. Nothing obvious in helm lint. kube-scheduler: "0/12 nodes are available: 12 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector."

maya: I traced it to our chart's nodeSelector helper. We use a small helper to coalesce cluster/global nodeSelector with per-release values. Example template: 
```yaml
{{- define "common.nodeSelector" }}
nodeSelector: {{ toYaml (coalesce .Values.nodeSelector .Values.global.nodeSelector) | nindent 8 }}
{{- end }}
```

maya: When we don't set `.Values.nodeSelector` in values.yaml the rendered manifest ends up with `nodeSelector: {}` in some cases (or `nodeSelector: null` depending on helm version). That seems to cause our gitops apply to explicitly clear the cluster default GPU label, so pods aren't scheduled on the GPUs.

ryan: Can you paste the exact `helm template` output showing the problematic bit?

maya: Yep, here's the snippet from `helm template` output: 
```yaml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: runtime
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {}
      containers:
      - name: runtime
        image: docker/re/runtime:2.4.0
```

jen: I think this is a classic rendering vs intent mismatch. Helm's `coalesce` will pick the first non-empty value; an empty map (`{}`) can be considered not set depending on how values are passed, or we end up with an explicit empty map object. `toYaml` then prints `{}`. Many controllers / kubectl apply will treat an explicit empty map as intent to remove keys from the live object.

sam: Quick fixes: either avoid rendering the `nodeSelector` key when it's empty, or ensure the values schema / CI always provides `{}` as a default so charts render consistently. My suggested helper: 
```gotemplate
{{- define "common.nodeSelector" }}
{{- $ns := merge .Values.global.nodeSelector .Values.nodeSelector }}
{{- if not (empty $ns) }}
nodeSelector: {{ toYaml $ns | nindent 8 }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```
This prevents `nodeSelector:` from appearing when there's nothing to set.

jen: Yea, `merge` plus `empty` or testing `kindIs` works. Another option: change values.schema.json so `nodeSelector` is explicitly an object with default `{}` — then `helm template` will consistently get `{}` (but you'll still have an explicit `{}` printed). I prefer the `if not (empty $ns)` approach to avoid producing the key at all.

ops-bot: CI note: `helm lint` and `ct lint` don't catch this pattern because it's a semantic/render issue, not a static lint error. Add a `helm template` based test in our pipeline: run `helm template` and assert `nodeSelector:` is absent when values are empty.

maya: Good point. The GitOps apply (flux) is treating the empty map as an intention to mutate the cluster-scoped label on the node pool; that caused the evictions and left GPU reserved capacity idle. This is causing cost + capacity issues — we had warm GPU nodes but no workloads scheduled, so Dedicated pools not utilized.

ryan: For rollout safety: add a pre-flight job in the pipeline that runs `helm template` + `kubeval`/`yamllint` and looks for empty maps for critical keys: `nodeSelector`, `affinity`, `tolerations`. If any found, fail the pipeline.

jen: Also add a small unit test using `helm-unittest` (or a simple `helm template` + grep) that checks that when `.Values.nodeSelector` and `.Values.global.nodeSelector` are unset the output does not contain `nodeSelector:` at the spec level. We should gate that in `charts/ci` in the GitOps repo.

sam: I'll propose the helper change in a PR and include two things: 1) helper change with `empty` guard 2) values.schema.json change to require object type and default to `{}` 3) CI test to catch regressions.

maya: Thanks — will link the problematic release, test in staging and then canary in eu-west before rolling to rest of regions. Also will check if any downstream charts rely on empty map semantics (unlikely).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canaries planned: runtime:2.4.0 -> eu-west (1/3), waiting on green.

ryan: Small note: for terraform-managed nodePools, we should also make sure our node labels are applied by the provisioning module so there's no drift. If a chart accidentally clears labels it's a provisioning+chart contract issue. Might be worth adding a constraint in the terraform module to reapply the GPU label if missing.

maya: Agree. Opening PR now: #7423 — includes helper + values.schema + ct/helm template test. Will tag reviewers: @jen @ryan @sam.

jen: Nice. Once merged, let's run the canary and add the `helm template` test to the default pipeline so we catch similar issues early. :+1:

sam: Also add a short note to infra runbook about this pattern (empty map vs no-key), so oncall can triage faster next time.

maya: Cool — thanks everyone.
